facts.value: Financial Outturn 2025/26 — a covering report to Executive. Sections 2.1–2.24 cover General Fund, HRA, capital programme and reserves; the treasury content in the covering report is a seven-bullet summary at §2.26 (p.8) that reads across from Appendix 6 (Treasury Management — Outturn 2025/26, doc 34151), also on disk here. This note treats Appendix 6 as the source for the loan-book, CFR and investment figures; the covering report as the source for headline aggregates and the operating narrative.
facts.note: Also relied on: Appendix 6 — Treasury Management — Outturn 2025/26 (doc 34151, on disk). The covering report explicitly names Appendix 6 as the source of its §2.26 summary. This paper was presented first to Finance and Corporate Overview Scrutiny Committee on 23 July 2026 (main paper p.1), then to Executive on 27 July 2026. Both meeting dates have passed (today 2026-08-15). No forward treasury meeting date is published in either document; the profile shows the Executive as the main finance body with a quarterly rhythm.

facts.value: £139.706m at 31 March 2026 (opening £129.960m + £9.898m HRA prudential borrowing − £380k MRP − £53k additional voluntary contributions + £281k movement on other debt/retentions). Net in-year increase £9.746m. GF share £17.100m; HRA share £122.606m.
facts.note: Appendix 6 p.1 CFR movement table and CFR split table. Also stated at main paper §2.26 p.8 as a single bullet (£139.706m). HRA-heavy — 87.8% of CFR sits in the HRA. In-year prudential borrowing supported new HRA Council Dwellings and the Crematorium at Shirebrook (Appendix 6 p.1 text).

facts.value: £76.800m PWLB, all fixed-rate maturity loans. No LOBOs, no market debt, no PFI/leases broken out in Appendix 6.
facts.note: Appendix 6 p.2 CFR-covered table and PWLB Borrowing table. Also main paper §2.26 p.8 ('The PWLB debt — £76.8m'). £2m of principal repaid in year; no new PWLB drawn. Opening PWLB £78.800m.

Appendix 6 p.2 CFR financing table ('Use of internal balances and reserves — 62,906'). Also stated at main paper §2.26 p.8 as 'Effective internal borrowing — £62.906m'. Balance-sheet identity: CFR 139.706 − PWLB 76.800 − OLTL 0 = internal 62.906. Ties exactly.

facts.value: CFR − external borrowing − other long-term liabilities = internal borrowing: £139.706m − £76.800m − £0 (none disclosed) = £62.906m. Matches the paper's own £62.906m to the pound.
facts.note: Appendix 6 p.2 (CFR financing table) contains all three terms explicitly and the identity is stated on the face of the table. The £281k in-year 'Movement on other debt – retentions' in the CFR movement table (Appendix 6 p.1) sits inside the £62.906m residual, not as a separately disclosed OLTL. Clean identity — no gap.

facts.value: PWLB debt at 31 March 2026 by maturity band (Appendix 6 p.2): 12 Months £3.000m; 1-2 years £7.800m; 2-5 years £12.000m; 5-10 years £24.000m; Over 10 years £30.000m. Total £76.800m. Movement from 31 March 2025: 12M +£1.0m; 1-2y +£4.8m; 2-5y −£3.8m; 5-10y +£1.0m; over 10y −£5.0m. Loans have rolled forward one bucket in most cases and £2m has been repaid.
facts.note: Verbatim from Appendix 6 p.2 PWLB Borrowing table. The 1-2y band tripled in the year (£3.0m → £7.8m) as loans rolled in from the 2-5y bucket. £10.8m matures inside two years — 14.06% of the £76.8m book.

facts.value: £2.655m in 2025/26 (cost split HRA/GF based on level of debt outstanding within CFR).
facts.note: Appendix 6 p.2 PWLB Interest text. Also main paper §2.26 p.8. No borrowing rate is quoted in the paper — the rate we use in the email is our file's £76.8m at 3.4203% weighted, not something the paper claims.

facts.value: £17.200m in Money Market Funds at 31 March 2026, all overnight (call accounts). Interest earned in year £992,157 at an average rate of 4.09%. Overnight balances held in Lloyds Bank general account.

summary.text:
Bolsover's 2025/26 Financial Outturn to Executive on 27 July 2026 is a covering report that reads across to Appendix 6 (Treasury Management — Outturn 2025/26) for the substantive treasury figures. Both are on disk. The covering report prints only a seven-bullet §2.26 summary; the CFR movement, CFR split, CFR financing, PWLB maturity profile, investment portfolio and treasury limits all sit in Appendix 6. There are no LOBOs, no market debt, no PFI or leases broken out — Appendix 6 discloses PWLB only alongside internal borrowing and overnight investments.

The reconciliation is unusually clean. CFR at 31 March 2026 is £139.706m (GF £17.100m, HRA £122.606m — 87.8% HRA), financed from £76.800m of PWLB and £62.906m of internal balances. The balance-sheet identity CFR − external borrowing − OLTL = internal borrowing lands on the printed £62.906m to the pound; no other long-term liabilities are broken out. Our PWLB file holds 17 loans at £76,800,000 weighted 3.4203%, and every one of Appendix 6's five maturity bands ties to the pound (£3.0m under 12 months, £7.8m in 1-2 years, £12.0m in 2-5 years, £24.0m in 5-10 years, £30.0m over 10). £2m of principal was repaid in year; no new PWLB was drawn.

The only band carrying a rate above the book's 3.4203% average is the 1-2 year bucket at a weighted 3.903%, and it is the second bucket to reprice. Combined with the 12-month bucket at 3.010%, £10.8m of book (14%) reprices inside two years — at today's certainty curve (4.95% at one year, 5.06% at two, DMO notice 314/26 PM on 2026-08-14) that's roughly a 1.3-1.4 point coupon step on the pieces coming due. The whole book prices to an indicative £7.04m discount on the same curve (9.2% of principal, 16 of 17 loans below par); indicative only, the DMO's quote is the only binding one. Investments are all overnight Money Market Funds held via Lloyds — £17.200m at year-end earning £992,157 across the year at a 4.09% average.

An email is drafted. The hook is the loan-book reconciliation itself: Appendix 6 to our file to the pound across all five buckets, plus the £10.8m near-term maturity story, plus the discount position as scoped-and-caveated context. Address is not published — the covering-report contact is 'Strategic Director of Finance and Section 151 Officer' as a title only, with no named officer and no email, and no addresses appear elsewhere in the paper. Draft goes to 'drafted — needs an address' pending a published officer email. Presentational point on Appendix 6's treasury-limits table (Authorised/Operational label order appears inverted relative to CIPFA convention) recorded internal-only; the substantive within-limits statement stands.

officer.subject: £10.8m of your PWLB matures inside two years — and Appendix 6 ties to the pound
officer.body:
Hi [OFFICER NAME],

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are a few thoughts on the 2025/26 outturn that went to Executive on 27 July. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it. Appendix 6 is unusually tidy by the standards of what we've read, and this is offered in that spirit rather than as a critique.

Starting with a favour Appendix 6 did us. We hold 17 PWLB loans against Bolsover, £76,800,000 at a weighted 3.4203%, and the principal ties to your Appendix 6 to the pound. So does every one of your five maturity bands — £3.0m under 12 months, £7.8m in 1-2 years, £12.0m in 2-5 years, £24.0m in 5-10 years, £30.0m over ten — with no loan crossing a bucket boundary between 31 March and today. The balance-sheet identity ties too: your £139.706m CFR less £76.800m of PWLB less nothing else disclosed equals the £62.906m of internal borrowing your paragraph 2.26 quotes. That is a set of books whose pieces fit together, which is not universal.

The reason we mention the buckets rather than just the total is that the 1-2 year band is the only one carrying a rate above your book average. Our file has that £7.8m at 3.903%, against the book's 3.4203%. On today's certainty curve, DMO notice 314/26 PM, two-year money is around 5.06% — Bank Rate is 3.75% and the one-year OIS is 4.11%, so the market is currently pricing rates up rather than down. The £3.0m under twelve months sits at 3.010% against 4.95% at one year on the same curve. Put together, £10.8m of book, 14%, reprices inside two years, at a coupon roughly 1.3 to 1.4 points above what it carries today. Not enormous in absolute terms on a £76.8m book; real all the same.

Since the outturn was framed at 31 March 2026, one thing worth noting is where the curve has moved to since then. Against 31 March, the ten-year is 0.11 higher and the twenty is 0.15 higher, the five-year barely moved (0.06), and the one-year is about 0.09 lower — so most of the curve is roughly where you set the strategy, with a small softening at the short end. Both fixings and the whole curve are at pwlbtoday.org/dashboard, and July's sector activity was £368m across 33 loans from 19 borrowers at a 5.02% average — that's at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity.

For context on the other half of the picture — we have your book at an indicative £7.04m discount to par on the same 2026-08-14 curve, sixteen of the seventeen loans below par and one above. Our engine prices every council's PWLB book daily at pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis, so the answer moves with the curve every morning. Indicative only — only the DMO can quote a binding settlement, we model no MRP or accounting treatment, and whether anything is worth doing turns on replacement cost we don't model.

On training, four fit Bolsover. PWLB break costs (mechanics and the live calculator) covers the discount position. Strategic PWLB borrowing is for whenever the next drawdown decision comes up — you took none in 2025/26, and the 1-2 year band is the piece that'll ask the question next. Interest rate risk goes to the same rollover question from the other side. And our Liability benchmark pathway, which is interactive and built on live data — worth a look given where CIPFA is heading with the Prudential and Treasury Codes. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy, and free accounts for the whole team.

And if you do find it useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/

Russell
https://www.linkedin.com/in/russelltew
